notes: CORPUS BUMP c2 -> c3 (TRAIN engine-authority revision, 2026-08-09). The c2 referee derived TRAIN legality from MoisanBot::can_train (rust/src/bin/yamo_orchard_live.rs:836, 'if n >= 2 || TOTAL_TURNS - view.turn <= 20 { return false; }'). That is ONE BOT'S SELF-RESTRAINT. The authority is rust/src/game/engine.rs::apply_train (525-568), which enforces NEITHER the two-worker cap NOR the final-20-turn guard: between the own-unit count at 527 (used only to price the bill at 528) and the spawn at 556-567 the only rejections are affordability (539-541) and an occupied shack (545-547). The c2 referee therefore forbade what the engine permits and would have silently rejected a candidate that trains a third worker. c3 removes both bot-derived restrictions and mirrors engine.rs alone. Permitting a third (and fourth, ...) worker changes many games; results are NOT comparable across the bump.

CORPUS BUMP c1 -> c2 (referee TRAIN repair, 2026-08-09). The referee now implements TRAIN and MINE and dispatches commands EXHAUSTIVELY: a verb with no handler terminates the run as GATE_UNREADY / unsupported_command instead of being silently discarded. Under c1 the referee silently dropped TRAIN and MINE, so every game in which the bot trained or mined was simulated against a world that never happened -- m040 seat 0 / seat 1 emitted TRAIN on 166 / 182 of 200 turns and still scored CLEAN. Results are NOT comparable across the bump; load_config refuses a config declaring a different version.

RAW/ABSOLUTE gate (owner ruling 2026-08-06): every detector D-1..D-9 episode blocks, inherited-from-parent or not, on every map, and P4 liveness has no parent exemption. The round-6 ROOT-A D-9 parent-differential gate and the D-1 inherited-report-only downgrade are both REMOVED. The parent run is still computed for the P3 orchard-inertness check (an absolute candidate==parent requirement, kept) and for diagnostics, but never exempts a candidate detector episode. trace_detectors is unmodified.

P4 ABSOLUTE terminal-state calibration (gate repair #2, 2026-08-06): a stall window blocks only over the turns in which the referee world state still offers the own player a resource action -- i.e. some own unit still carries something to bank/plant, or some plant still stands on a cell an own unit can walk to (harvest/chop) -- so a stall that begins after the world is exhausted for the rest of the game is excused while any stall of >= liveness_window LIVE turns, mid-game or running to the sim horizon, still blocks. The predicate reads only the candidate's own transcript (static map + plants + own units): no parent reference, no all-WAIT command heuristic.

SOURCE PORTABILITY REPAIR (2026-08-12, against chatgpt_1's M3a review 20260811T230000Z: REVISION_REQUIRED -- SOURCE REPLAY NOT PORTABLE). `candidate.source` and `parent.source` previously held absolute paths under /tmp/claude-1000/<session-id>/scratchpad and /home/tarstars, which exist on no clean runner and not on this host once the session scratchpad is reaped. Each entry now carries `source_git` = {commit, path}: an IMMUTABLE commit id, not a moving branch. The replay materialises the blob from that commit into a temp dir and re-checks it against the `sha256` pin above before compiling, so provenance is fixed by the commit and content by the digest. `source` now holds the repo-relative path for the record; a direct panel run that does not materialise will fail loudly on a missing path rather than silently depend on a scratch directory. NOTHING measured changes: same seeds, same mixes, same corpus_version, same instrument_version, same sha256 pins, same run_identity.

OUTPUT PATHS (same repair). `bin_cache_dir` and `games_dir` were absolute paths under the same session scratchpad. They are now names resolved relative to this config's own directory by fuzz_panel.resolve(), so no absolute host path remains anywhere in this config. Both are untracked build/output directories; the replay does not read either, and overrides them into a temp dir regardless.
